note: Rewritten from Roonwal & Chhotani 1989 (Fauna of India, Isoptera, Vol. 1, species 48); original in English; the OCR is clear. The pronotum length of the pseudoworker is printed "1.(X)" in the OCR and is recorded here as 1.00 mm, as reflected in the range in the text.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule yellow to straw coloured, antennae yellow to pale yellow, labrum straw coloured, base of the mandibles deep straw and the rest dark brown; pronotum, tibiae, tarsi and dorsal abdomen yellow, femora and sternites yellowish white; head and body rather densely hairy. Body length (with wings) about 10.5—11.5 mm. Head capsule almost square, moderately densely covered with short hairs; length to the mandibular base (1.05—1.20 mm) nearly equal to the maximum width including the compound eyes (1.16—1.20 mm); convex in the middle in side view; frons sloping gently forwards, without a median depression; Y suture indistinct. Compound eyes black, large, nearly circular, maximum diameter including the eye sclerite 0.48—0.59 mm, close to the antennae. Ocelli small, almost oval, maximum diameter 0.18—0.25 mm, whitish and translucent, oblique and elongate vertically, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 16—18-segmented, segment 4 shortest. Anteclypeus rather long, trapezoidal, whitish, hairless; postclypeus almost square, darker than the frons, anterior margin with 2 pairs of hairs; labrum almost square, widest in the anterior 1/3 (length 0.35—0.55 mm), anterior margin almost rounded, anterior part and clypeal surface with long and short hairs. Pronotum wider than the head width including the eyes, flat, almost square (width 1.55—1.60 mm, length 1.0—1.10 mm), anterior margin concave, sides almost rounded, posterior margin almost straight. Legs short and slender, densely hairy; tibial spur formula 3:3:3; tarsi 4-segmented; no arolium between the claws. Forewing length 9.5—10.0 mm, hind wing length 9.0—9.5 mm; the wing scale longer than the hind wing scale; costa, subcosta, radius and radial sector of the forewing thick and strongly chitinised, parallel near the anterior margin; media and cubitus weakly chitinised; subcosta long, meeting the marginal vein at about 1/4 of the wing membrane; radius meeting the marginal vein beyond the middle; radial sector giving off 5—6 branches to the marginal vein after the radius and marginal vein have joined; media arising from the cubitus at the wing-scale suture, with veins fading towards the radial sector and the cubitus; cubitus with about 10 branches reaching the posterior margin. Subcosta absent in the hind wing, the media arising from the radial sector within the wing membrane.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule reddish brown, paler anteriorly and posteriorly; base of the antennae dark brown, becoming paler towards the apex; labrum brownish; postmentum darker; thorax and legs pale brown; abdomen pale straw; head and body rather densely covered with short hairs. Body length about 7.4—9.5 mm. Head capsule rectangular, distinctly longer than wide (length to the mandibular base 2.02—2.47 mm, width 1.57—1.95 mm); sides almost parallel, slightly narrowed anteriorly; frons sloping in front, the median depression extending backwards to the middle of the head; Y suture indistinct. Compound eyes small, oval (length 0.15—0.23 mm), black, close against the antennae, the distance between eye and antenna 0.18 mm, about equal to the maximum diameter of the compound eye; no ocelli. Antennae 11—14-segmented; antennal carinae large and upturned, covering the basal segment; segment 4 shortest; rather densely hairy, denser towards the apex. Anteclypeus weakly developed, almost trapezoidal, hairless; postclypeus almost square, dark, separated from the frons by a narrow transverse depression, anterior margin with 2 pairs of hairs. Labrum tongue-shaped to pear-shaped, distinctly wider than long (width 0.45—0.55 mm, length 0.25—0.35 mm), anterior margin and clypeal surface with short hairs, anterior margin either pointed or rounded. Mandibles rather long, stout at the base and raised, about 2/3 of the head length to the mandibular base (length 1.4—1.5 mm); left mandible with 4—5 marginal teeth, right mandible with 2 marginal teeth. Postmentum short to long, club-shaped (median length 1.4—1.6 mm), widest in the anterior 1/3 (maximum width 0.55—0.70 mm), narrowing anteriorly to a broad, almost convex anterior margin and posteriorly to a narrower waist (waist width 0.30—0.35 mm), then expanding again into a rather convex posterior margin. Pronotum almost square, rather densely covered with short hairs; anterior margin deeply concave, without a median notch; anterior lateral corners rounded; posterior margin almost straight. Legs slender and short, hairy; tibial spur formula 3:3:3; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen long, each tergite with 2 rows of hairs; cerci short, 2-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pseudoworker: head capsule straw coloured, labrum and antennae paler, mandibles deep straw with the inner margin dark brown; pronotum, legs and body yellowish white; head and body rather densely hairy. Body length 6.5—7.0 mm. Head capsule almost circular, length and width nearly equal (width 1.4—1.5 mm, length 1.3—1.4 mm); compound eyes degenerate, small, black, almost circular, flush with the head surface; no ocelli. Antennae 13—15-segmented and hairy, segments 3—5 nearly equal and shortest. Anteclypeus trapezoidal, whitish, rather large; postclypeus almost square, darker than the frons, anterior margin with a few short hairs; labrum and mandibles as in the alate. Pronotum almost square (width 1.6—1.7 mm, length 0.70—1.00 mm), densely hairy; anterior margin concave.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The species builds fine narrow longitudinal galleries in wood, the galleries filled with dry, compacted, loose faecal pellets, as in Cryptotermes; it has been recorded from several tree species (including the jujube Zizyphus jujuba and apple), but is not a serious pest. In laboratory colonies the alates emerge in June—August (months 6—8); the numerical ratio of alates, soldiers and pseudoworkers is 1:5:94, and continuous parthenogenesis has been recorded.
